articles.title: DOJ SEEKS $1.17 BILLION IN USDC TIED TO BINANCE HACK
articles.summary: The DOJ filed a civil forfeiture complaint for about $1.17B in USDC across 36 addresses on 18 blockchains, attributing the theft on October 29 to North Korea's Lazarus Group/APT38, and separately asked a judge to keep the assets restrained since the November 12 order may lapse. Circle blocked the USDC but can't move the original tokens, so it agreed to issue equivalent new USDC to the US if forfeiture is granted. The DOJ says over $2.9B in crypto has been frozen, seized, or returned since the theft. Binance puts losses at about $6.34B, says it replenished them, and also won a $6.5B worldwide freezing order in Abu Dhabi.

articles.title: CFTC STAFF SAY BTC AND ETH CAN COUNT TOWARD DERIVATIVES FIRMS' OPEX
articles.summary: A staff advisory says swap execution facilities, clearing organizations, and designated contract markets may count BTC, ETH, and payment stablecoins, subject to a haircut, toward the requirement to hold a year of operating expenses. Crypto doesn't qualify as cash or very liquid securities, so it can't count toward the separate liquidity requirement, and the advisory isn't enforceable. The CFTC also published a final rule creating a reporting framework for certain event contracts, replacing no-action letters.

articles.title: PRIVY ADDS VERIFIABLE ENCLAVE ATTESTATIONS FOR WALLET OPERATIONS
articles.summary: Privy added verifiable enclave attestations to its wallet infrastructure, giving developers cryptographic proof that sensitive wallet operations executed inside AWS Nitro enclaves. The feature shifts the security model from operator trust to cryptographic verification, letting any external party confirm that key operations ran in an isolated, hardened compute environment. This closes a gap common in MPC and embedded wallet providers, where users had to accept security claims without cryptographic evidence.

articles.title: VISA LAUNCHES CLI AGENT WALLET ON TEMPO AND MPP
articles.summary: Visa expanded its Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP) to agent wallets and task marketplaces, and launched Visa CLI, an experimental agent wallet for OUSD built on Tempo and the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP), available to US users as a connector to major agent platforms. TAP lets users attach a Visa card to their agent wallet, register that agent in Visa's Agent Directory, and have the verified agent complete paid tasks spanning video creation, music, gaming, surveys, and market research, with earnings settled in OUSD. The expansion follows TAP's October 2025 debut and existing pilots with Cloudflare and Akamai for e-commerce authentication, plus a B2B pilot with Bill.com and Billtrust for agent-verified invoice payments. Visa is positioning its 5 billion existing payment credentials as the accountability layer for agent transactions and is soliciting integration partners among agent wallet builders, personal assistants, and marketplace operators.

articles.title: TASK MARKETS: THE FINAL FORM OF AGENTIC COMMERCE
articles.summary: Agentic commerce is converging on the task, a verified unit of completed work. This article outlines three layers: single agent with skills and MCP, pay-per-call, and task markets for complex work needing judgement and verification. Coinbase is building open standards on its own rails while Stripe is closed and extends its existing business, with Tempo as the settlement layer that could weaken harness lock-in. Daydreams' TaskMarket on Base and Tempo (ERC-8195) has 16,500 registered agents, 1,843 tasks, and about $3,756 paid out, and Visa's new CLI wallet integrates it.

articles.title: WHAT'S A BLOCK, AND HOW BIG CAN IT GET?
articles.summary: Under Glamsterdam's 60M gas limit, skipped EIP-7702 authorizations, not calldata, represent the worst-case block-size attack vector, packing 17.0 bytes per 1k gas and producing 1.81 MiB EL blocks, about 2x what calldata can achieve. This creates a structural conflict with FOCIL (EIP-7805): a transaction satisfying gas constraints may breach the 8 MiB EL byte cap when appended, leaving builders unable to honor attesters' inclusion expectations despite valid gas usage. The proposed re-encoding patch fails in four edge cases, so the author argues for pricing every payload byte in gas via EIP-8131 and EIP-8279 plus deposit-request metering, with a capped gas limit (256M without those EIPs, 500M with them). This bounds worst-case envelope size and gives the CL a deterministic maximum: max_envelope_size = C + ceil(1.25 x gas_limit / 64).

articles.title: HOW CAN CRYPTO NEOBANKS WIN?
articles.summary: Weekly crypto card spend exceeds $300M, up almost 200% year over year, but the top 5 of the 20 largest programs hold 86% of the last 30 days' spend, with RedotPay alone over 46%. Users spend only $0.65 to $0.75 per $1 topped up, treating apps as savings, and EtherFi and KAST offer 7 to 9% APY on stablecoin deposits. After cashback, most programs earn under 1% of spend while paying 2 to 3%, and card infrastructure from providers like Rain is commoditized. Differentiation will come from local rails, multi-currency settlement, and owning the yield source, with EtherFi's Aave V4 loans over $47M and Phantom earning over $20M in perps builder fees.

articles.title: XMR1 COLLAPSES 99% AFTER DEPLOYER KEY STOLEN IN WEB HOST BREACH
articles.summary: XMR1, Wagyu's wrapped Monero token on Hyperliquid, fell from about $500 to $1 in 30 minutes after an attacker extracted 5.2 million tokens from the deployer wallet and sold 364,000 of them to 388 buyers for $13.5 million, converting the proceeds to about 7,350 ETH. Wagyu founder PerpetualCow attributed the breach to Icelandic host 1984.hosting, claiming the deployer private key persisted on a deleted server whose logs the host retained, with 1984 confirming a broad cyberattack on its infrastructure without naming Wagyu or disclosing whether customer data was taken. The attacker seeded the exploit wallet via Tornado Cash minutes before the drain, and the same deployer account still controls ZEC1, a wrapped Zcash token carrying identical centralization risk. PerpetualCow pledged direct refunds to affected holders with no relaunch timeline given. The incident is Wagyu's second reported breach in two months and follows the service's appearance in ZachXBT's tracing of a $106 million theft routed through the platform.

articles.title: CHAINFLIP CONFIRMS $12M VAULT HACK, OFFERS ATTACKER 10% BOUNTY
articles.summary: Chainflip confirmed attackers drained approximately $12 million from its vaults, comprising 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3.25 million USDC, and 758,141 USDT, more than doubling the initial $4.86 million estimate.

articles.title: BITCOIN ETFS POST $1.79B WEEKLY OUTFLOW, THIRD-LARGEST ON RECORD
articles.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $1.79B in net outflows last week, the third-largest weekly total since the product category launched in January 2024, extending a four-week redemption streak to $4.34B.
